title: Zahirah MacWilson apologises for religious insensitivity remark
text:

 News Finance More Mail Search the web Advertisement Advertisement Return to homepage Zahirah MacWilson apologises for religious insensitivity remark
 Heidi Hsia Mon, 2 November 2026 at 6:54 am UTC 1 min read Add Yahoo as a preferred source to see more of our stories on Google. 2 Nov - Zahirah MacWilson has recently released a statement of apology, after making a comment about seasonal and religious festivals that was deemed insensitive by many.
 The whole issue started after the actress posted on Instagram Story an image of a Halloween decoration that she saw, opining that it was the most ridiculous celebration even back when she was living abroad for 20 years.
 She then commented that she considered Christmas, Easter and Halloween as "all strange celebrations" involving kids dressing up and "sitting on old men's lap," "worshipping some demonic/satanic/supernatural character or death".
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement It was quickly slammed by many, who said that her comments are culturally and religiously insensitive, especially for one living in a multicultural country.
 In response, the actress posted an apology on 1 November, apologising for offending people and saying that she had quickly taken the post down as to not cause any more wrong assumptions.
 "It was never my intention to hurt anyone's beliefs. I am still in the process of learning about faith and beliefs, and since then, I've done research not just on mine, but on others too," she stated. "I found it strange that the facts I've read contradict what I observe. My point in the post was not to pick on anyone, but rather to express a questioning understanding."
 "Islam has taught me to be just, kind, and fair, and not to insult others," she added.
 The actress admitted previously that she is on the journey to understand her own spirituality
